title: Observability & Telemetry: Bounded Data Use Addendum (Template)
summary: Template addendum to govern collection, use, retention, access, and export of telemetry and observability data generated through a vendor integration. Intended to be attached to a primary services agreement or data processing agreement when the vendor will receive or process telemetry logs, metrics, traces, or application-level diagnostics.
body:
Purpose
This Addendum ("Addendum") defines specific controls and contractual limits on Observability and Telemetry Data that the Vendor may collect, store, process, or export in connection with providing services to the Customer. It supplements and, to the extent inconsistent, governs over the parties' Master Services Agreement and any Data Processing Agreement.

1. Definitions
For the purposes of this Addendum: 
- "Observability and Telemetry Data" means logs, metrics, traces, spans, profiling data, health-check heartbeats, runtime diagnostics, instrumentation payloads, and related metadata generated by the Customer's systems, applications, or users (including any system-generated identifiers and performance counters) that Vendor collects to provide monitoring, alerting, debugging, or capacity planning services. 
- "PII" means personal data or personally identifiable information as defined under applicable law. 
- "Anonymized/Aggregated Data" means data transformed so that it cannot reasonably be re-identified to an individual or single customer instance without the use of additional information that is kept separately.
- "Telemetry Whitelist" means the specific list of telemetry types and fields the Customer permits the Vendor to ingest (see Appendix A).

2. Scope and Applicability
This Addendum applies to all Observability and Telemetry Data the Vendor receives, ingests, stores, processes, or exports in providing the services described in the Agreement. Unless expressly permitted in writing by the Customer, Vendor shall not collect any telemetry beyond the Telemetry Whitelist.

3. Permitted Purposes
Vendor shall only collect or use Observability and Telemetry Data for the following purposes ("Permitted Purposes"): 
(a) Providing the monitoring, alerting, diagnostics, and service-level reporting agreed in the Agreement;
(b) Root cause analysis and troubleshooting of incidents affecting the Customer's service;
(c) Capacity planning and service optimization for the Customer's dedicated resources;
(d) Security monitoring for indicators of compromise affecting the Customer environment, but subject to the limitations in Section 6 (PII and Sensitive Data).
Any other use (including product development, model training, marketing analytics, or benchmarking) requires the Customer's prior written consent and, when applicable, an amendment to the Agreement that specifies data minimization and compensation terms.

4. Data Minimization and Field-Level Controls
(a) Telemetry Whitelist: Vendor shall only ingest fields and event types listed in the Telemetry Whitelist (Appendix A). The parties shall review the whitelist during onboarding and at least annually.
(b) Field Redaction: Vendor shall implement field-level redaction at collection time for any fields that may contain PII or sensitive configuration details (e.g., secrets, full URLs with query parameters, cryptographic keys). Redaction rules must be configurable and enforceable by Customer.
(c) Sampling & Rate Controls: Where high-volume telemetry is involved, Vendor shall support sampling and rate limiting as configured by Customer, with documented sampling policies and expected data loss rate communicated before changes are applied.

5. Pseudonymization, Aggregation, and Anonymization
(a) Pseudonymization: Where short-lived identifiers are necessary for correlation (traces/spans), Vendor shall replace user-identifying fields with stable pseudonyms within the minimum retention period; mapping keys must be stored separately and protected with least privilege.
(b) Aggregation: For long-term analytics, Vendor shall provide aggregated views (e.g., 1m/5m buckets) that prevent row-level reconstruction of user activity.
(c) Re-identification Prohibition: Vendor shall not attempt to re-identify Anonymized/Aggregated Data or combine telemetry with external datasets to identify a person or customer's internal identifiers without Customer's explicit consent.

6. Sensitive Data and PII
(a) Prohibition: Vendor shall not collect sensitive personal data (e.g., health, race, biometric data) unless strictly necessary for a Permitted Purpose and authorized by Customer in writing.
(b) Minimization: Any PII collected must be minimized to the least possible granularity and stored using encryption at rest and in transit with strong algorithms (AES-256 or equivalent).
(c) Legal Requests: If Vendor receives a legal or regulatory request for telemetry that includes PII, Vendor shall redirect such requests to Customer whenever legally permissible and provide Customer prompt notice per the Agreement.

7. Data Retention and Deletion
(a) Retention Schedule: Telemetry shall be retained according to the Retention Schedule in Appendix B. Short-term raw telemetry ("Hot" data) retention shall not exceed 90 days by default unless the Customer configures a different duration in writing. 
(b) Archival and Aggregated Retention: Aggregated or rolled-up metrics may be retained for longer periods (e.g., 24 months) where noted in Appendix B.
(c) Deletion on Termination: Upon termination or earlier request, Vendor shall (i) delete Customer telemetry and mapping keys within 30 days unless legal hold applies, and (ii) provide a certificate of deletion. Any backups containing telemetry shall be overwritten/rotated pursuant to agreed timelines.
body_continued:
8. Access Controls, Logging, and Operational Security
(a) Principle of Least Privilege: Only authorized personnel with a documented business need shall have access to raw telemetry. Role-based access controls and just-in-time access mechanisms are required.
(b) Access Auditing: Vendor shall maintain immutable access logs for all accesses to raw telemetry and mapping keys and retain those logs for at least 12 months. These logs must be exportable to Customer or an agreed SIEM on request.
(c) Strong Authentication: Access to vendor consoles or APIs that expose telemetry must require MFA and support SSO integrations with Customer identity providers.

9. Encryption and Transport Security
All Observability and Telemetry Data shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2+ (recommend TLS 1.3) and encrypted at rest. Key management practices must be documented; if Customer opts for customer-managed keys (CMK), Vendor must support integration with Customer KMS for encryption of telemetry storage.

10. Export, Sharing, and Subprocessors
(a) Export Controls: Vendor shall not export telemetry outside of permitted jurisdictions without prior Customer consent and applicable data residency commitments.
(b) Subprocessors: Vendor shall disclose subprocessors that will access telemetry and provide standard subprocessors addendum terms. Customer reserves the right to object to a subprocessor for legitimate security/privacy reasons; upon objection Vendor shall cease use of that subprocessor for Customer data or propose a mitigation plan.
(c) Third-party Sharing: Vendor may not share raw telemetry with third parties for their own purposes (e.g., analytics vendors, model training) unless Customer provides prior written consent. Aggregated non-identifying telemetry may be used for benchmarking only if explicit consent is obtained.

11. Monitoring Integrations and SIEM
Where Vendor integrates telemetry into Customer SIEM or security tooling, Vendor shall support field mappings that allow redaction or pseudonymization and provide documentation for parsers. Vendor shall maintain a change log of parser updates and notify Customer 14 days before breaking changes.
body_continued_2:
12. Incident Management and Forensics
(a) Incident Notification: Vendor shall notify Customer within 24 hours of discovery of any security incident that materially affects Customer telemetry confidentiality or integrity and provide timely updates.
(b) Forensics Support: Vendor shall preserve relevant telemetry and provide forensic access to Customer or a mutually approved third-party investigator under NDA; forensic access requests must be time-limited and audited.

13. Audit Rights and Evidence
(a) Right to Audit: Customer shall have the right to audit Vendor's controls relevant to telemetry handling once annually or after a material incident, via on-site inspections or a mutually agreed third-party audit report (SOC 2 Type II or equivalent).
(b) Evidence: Vendor shall provide evidence of configurations, retention schedules, redaction rules, and access logs within 10 business days of Customer request.

14. Metrics & Billing Data Separation
Vendor shall segregate telemetry used for operational monitoring from metadata used for billing or usage metering. Billing data exports shall not contain raw observability traces or PII fields unless explicitly requested and authorized by Customer.

15. Changes to Telemetry Processing
Vendor shall provide at least 30 days' prior notice for material changes to collection, retention, storage location, or subprocessors affecting telemetry. Any material change that increases privacy risk requires Customer approval before deployment.

16. Remedies and Liability
Vendor acknowledges that unauthorized use of telemetry that results in Customer harm may cause irreparable damage. Remedies available under the Agreement (including injunctive relief) apply; liability caps shall not apply to willful misconduct or gross negligence related to telemetry misuse.

17. Termination and Transition Assistance
Upon termination, Vendor shall provide transition assistance to export telemetry in a machine-readable format and delete retained telemetry per Section 7. Transition assistance shall include one export of historical aggregated metrics in CSV/Parquet formats unless otherwise agreed.

Appendices
Appendix A: Telemetry Whitelist (example)
- System metrics: cpu_percent, mem_used_percent, disk_io_ops (sampled)
- Service metrics: request_latency_ms_p50, request_latency_ms_p95, error_rate
- Traces: span_id, trace_id (pseudonymized), service_name, operation_name, duration, status_code
- Logs: severity, timestamp, message (with PII redaction), source_service, environment_tag
- Avoid: full request bodies, query strings with parameters, Authorization headers, full IP addresses unless allowed by Customer

Appendix B: Retention Schedule (example)
- Raw traces and logs (hot): 30–90 days default (Customer configurable)
- Aggregated metrics (1m/5m): 12–24 months
- Long-term aggregates (daily/week/month): 36 months max unless otherwise approved
- Mapping keys for pseudonyms: retained only for correlation window, default 30 days then rotated/expired

Appendix C: Onboarding Checklist (operational)
- Agree Telemetry Whitelist and sampling rules
- Configure field-level redaction and verify via test payloads
- Establish key management (CMK or vendor-managed)
- Enable access logging and invite Customer SIEM integration test
- Define retention settings and deletion verification process

Execution
This Addendum is executed by the parties' authorized representatives and becomes effective as of the Effective Date of the underlying Agreement or on the date signed below, whichever is later.

Notes for negotiators:
- Be explicit about whether IP addresses are allowed; often acceptable if truncated or hashed and only for security use-cases.
- Consider offering Customer an option for on-prem telemetry collector (agent) so raw logs never leave Customer environment.
- If vendor needs telemetry for product improvement, require separate opt-in program with clear anonymization and compensation or discounted pricing.

End of Addendum.
